headline: I build AI agents and automations that run every day.
lede: A person approves anything that goes public. The rest runs, reports and recovers on its own.
about: Before DarkoApp I spent six years running Nxgen Media, a VFX company in India and the USA, and sold it in 2025. I started in film and TV production.
work_intro: All of these are my own work, built with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cline). I own the architecture, testing, deployment and daily operation.

facts.text: A content agent picks a topic, writes a script, checks its own logic, renders slides and video, and schedules posts every day.
Every post waits for a person to approve, reject or redo it in Telegram before it can publish.
Posts go to X, LinkedIn, Bluesky and Telegram through the Postiz and Buffer APIs, with captions fitted to each platform's limits.
Health checks run every 15 minutes and send one alert per issue per day.
Every deploy ships with a rollback image, a database snapshot and a config backup.
Each feature starts as a written plan with its own test suite; the content engine's latest suite has 70 checks.
I moved video rendering to an owned GPU over a Tailscale private network, removing about $2.50 of cloud GPU cost per video, and the bot asks before it spends money on cloud GPUs.
I built and run DarkoApp, a live AI web and mobile app on Supabase (Postgres, row-level security, edge functions) with Stripe billing.
The DarkoApp engine classifies intent, streams answers and switches to a second model when the first times out.
I built retrieval (RAG) with embeddings and vector search over about 140 curated passages, plus a probe tool that shows what a question retrieves.
GitHub Actions smoke tests call the live AI engine and compare results with a saved baseline before and after prompt changes.
I connected Supabase, Stripe, Telegram, Postiz, Buffer, Gemini, DeepSeek, Venice, RunPod, Replicate and GitHub Actions with REST calls, webhooks and scheduled jobs.
I use n8n in my content pipeline and build the same triggers, webhooks, retries and approval steps in code when a workflow needs more control.
I built an MCP server in Node and TypeScript, with 38 tests, so AI assistants can call DarkoApp's engine as a tool.
I built approval-gated publishing: a draft-to-published lifecycle enforced in SQL, with prerendered SEO pages.
I run a ComfyUI render engine on an RTX 3090 for image, lip-synced video, voice and music generation (Wan 2.2, MiniMax, Flux, Qwen-Image).
I trained a Wan 2.2 character LoRA to keep one identity consistent across shots.
My pipelines produce 4–5 pieces of image, video and voice content a day (ComfyUI, n8n).

I built a job search assistant (Python, Streamlit, Groq) that searches Indeed, LinkedIn and about 300 company career boards, scores each posting on three models in parallel, and tailors a resume, cover letter and portfolio page per job.
My job assistant fills application forms in a visible browser from saved answers and never clicks Submit on its own.
I built a 3,000-contact outreach database with automated newsletter campaigns and ongoing sourcing.
I run open-weight models (Qwen, Gemma) locally and compare self-hosted and hosted models on cost, latency and quality.
I used GA4 bounce-rate data to choose the homepage headline for darkoapp.com.
I build with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cline) and own the architecture, testing, deployment and operations.
I founded and ran Nxgen Media, a VFX company in India and the USA, from 2019 to 2025, won and delivered client projects, and sold the company.
I am board treasurer and social media manager for VES Georgia, the Visual Effects Society chapter, and ran virtual voting and technical support for the VES Awards.
I worked on film productions in India from 2011 to 2019 as an assistant editor and assistant director, and wrote original screenplays registered with the writers' union in India.
From 2020 to 2023 I was a Health and Safety PA on US productions including Servant (Season 4), The Wonder Years and Descendants: The Rise of Red.

projects.title: Content automation engine
projects.sub: Daily social content, from topic to scheduled post, with approval on every piece.
points: Two formats from one script: chat-style Reels and 8-slide carousels. Topics come from a 110-topic bank in Supabase, and anti-repetition rules reject hooks and lessons used recently.
Every post waits for approve, reject or redo in Telegram. Captions are fitted per platform, such as Bluesky's 300-character limit.
Health check every 15 minutes with de-duplicated alerts. Each deploy ships with a rollback image, a database snapshot and 70 automated checks.
Heavy video renders moved to an owned GPU reached over a Tailscale private network, removing about $2.50 of cloud GPU cost per video. The bot asks before it spends money on cloud GPUs.
projects.stack: Python · Docker Compose · Linux VPS · Telegram Bot API · Supabase · headless Chromium · ffmpeg · Postiz · Buffer · Tailscale

projects.title: DarkoApp
projects.sub: A live AI communication coach for dating, on web and mobile.
points: Expo / React Native + web in TypeScript, on Supabase: Postgres with row-level security, auth, Deno edge functions and scheduled jobs. Stripe Checkout through the raw REST API.
Automatic switch to a second model when the first times out. A normalizer and leak guard keep structured output from breaking the interface.
Retrieval over about 140 curated passages. I purged around 2,400 noisy OCR rows after testing what questions actually retrieved.
GitHub Actions smoke tests call the live engine and compare results with a saved baseline before and after every prompt change.
projects.stack: TypeScript · Expo · Supabase · Postgres · DeepSeek · Gemini · Stripe · GitHub Actions · Netlify · Astro

projects.title: Job search assistant
projects.sub: Finds, ranks and prepares job applications, including this page.
points: Searches Indeed and LinkedIn, plus about 300 company career boards through the public Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby APIs.
Scores every posting against my resume on three Groq models in parallel to stay inside free-tier rate limits.
Writes a tailored resume, cover letter and portfolio page for each job. Every claim on the page comes from a bank of my own verified facts.
Fills application forms in a visible browser from saved answers. It never clicks Submit.
projects.stack: Python · Streamlit · Groq · LangChain · python-jobspy · Playwright · GitHub Pages

projects.title: Publishing platform and MCP server
projects.sub: Approval-gated publishing, plus a tool that AI assistants can call directly.
points: Planned and built in 8 phases. Lifecycle rules live in SQL, and a test fails if the app's copy of those rules drifts.
Pages are prerendered with the public key, so row-level security makes drafts unreadable by design.
MCP server in Node / TypeScript (Streamable HTTP) with 38 tests and separate client and server tokens.
The social integration was verified end to end with real draft posts on X, Telegram and Bluesky before anything went public.
projects.stack: Node · TypeScript · MCP · Supabase migrations · SQL triggers · Postiz API

projects.title: Generative media lab
projects.sub: Image, video, voice and music generation, run locally and in the cloud.
points: ComfyUI render engine on an RTX 3090 with lip-synced character video, Wan 2.2, Qwen-Image-Edit and Flux.
Trained a Wan 2.2 character LoRA (ai-toolkit, 2,000 steps) to keep one identity consistent across shots.
Cloud engines when needed: RunPod serverless, Replicate and Venice. A thermal guard pauses GPU jobs at 83 °C and resumes at 70 °C.
An earlier storyboard-to-video pipeline sent each shot to the right engine: Wan for motion, InfiniteTalk for talking shots.
projects.stack: ComfyUI · Wan 2.2 · MiniMax · Flux · Qwen-Image · Seedream · Seedance · RunPod · Replicate · Venice
